tieuDeEn: Like spring grass we play in the yard each day, but we also think about how to make our parents happy: grown-ups have more worries than joys, so when Dad is worried we show love, and when Mum is sad we don't make a fuss.

dichXuoi.vi: Chúng mình như ngọn cỏ xuân, ngày ngày vui chơi trước sân. Trong lòng luôn nghĩ: làm sao cho cha mẹ vui?
dichXuoi.en: We are like spring grass, playing in the yard every day. In our hearts we always wonder: how can we make our parents happy?

dichXuoi.vi: Người lớn ít khi được vui, mà lo buồn thì nhiều. Khi cha lo nghĩ, con nên thương cha; khi mẹ buồn, con đừng quấy mẹ.
dichXuoi.en: Grown-ups rarely have time to be happy and often have worries. When Dad is worried, we should show him love; when Mum is sad, we shouldn't bother her.

cauHoi.hoi: Theo bài thơ, cuộc sống người lớn thế nào?

keBoMe: Hỏi bố mẹ: điều gì làm bố mẹ mệt hoặc lo lắng khi đi làm?
Khi thấy bố hoặc mẹ buồn, con thường làm gì?
Con nghĩ ra một việc nhỏ nào để bố mẹ vui ngay hôm nay?

la.de: Viết đoạn văn 5–7 câu: Làm cho cha mẹ vui lòng.
goiY: Vì sao em giống như cỏ xuân?
Người lớn thường có những lo buồn gì?
Khi cha lo, mẹ buồn, em nên làm gì?
Kể một lần em làm cho bố mẹ vui.

baiHoc: Vui chơi nhưng luôn nghĩ cách cho cha mẹ vui.
Cha mẹ có nhiều lo toan, vất vả.
Cha lo – con thương; mẹ buồn – con chớ quấy.
baiHocEn: Play happily, but always think of how to make your parents happy. Grown-ups have many worries. When Dad worries, show love; when Mum is sad, don't make a fuss.
viecTot: Tuần này, khi bố mẹ đi làm về, em chào, mời nước và tự giác làm xong việc của mình mà không cần nhắc.
en: Cô Hà welcomes you to lesson eighteen of “Lên Tám”. Last time she compared you to young spring grass soaking up your parents' warm love. Today we'll see how, while playing in the yard every day, you should think and act to bring your parents the most joy. Listen to the next two verses.
Now we are like spring grass, playing in the yard every day; deep in our hearts we wonder how to make our parents happy.
Happy times are few, worries are easy to see; when Dad worries, we should show love; when Mum is sad, we shouldn't make a fuss.

The child in the poem knows himself well: at eight, it's the age to play and run freely in the safe yard. But he doesn't just play selfishly – he keeps a very grown-up thought: how should I behave and study so that my parents feel proud and smile whenever they see me? “Tấc dạ” means the heart inside.

The next verse reminds us of grown-ups' hardships: few joys, many worries. Parents work outside with many cares and much tiredness to support the family. So the poem teaches: when Dad is worried, show love by keeping quiet and helping with small jobs; when Mum is tired or sad, don't cry, demand things or sulk. Your understanding and self-discipline are the best tonic to take away your parents' tiredness.
